request: A tool that takes a subject and level, researches to find a sufficient curriculum, and uses recursive subagents to develop lessons with learning goals and, where applicable, visualizations. Lessons should be structured in 20 minute chunks when possible, but flexibility is fine when merited. If there is a well regarded explanation on a topic on a video hosting site that would be comprehensible, link to it. Otherwise, generate an explanation that is appropriate for the user's current level of understanding. These should be as terse as possible while still remaining usable. At the end of each section is an evaluation structured as a chat. Evaluations should be narrative and Socratic where applicable. Exercises should require the user to fully specify a solution to a problem. The goal is to know the material well enough to thoroughly understand wikis and papers, sharpen one's understanding of the world, and use it to build in collaboration with AI agents. There's no need to memorize exact formulas or computation that would be abstracted out in practice. Once the evaluator agent is satisfied that the user understands the material, the section is marked as completed. An evaluation failure should begin a discussion explaining the misunderstanding and re-evaluation until passing. Reevaluation should ask the question from a different angle if possible to avoid simple memorization. Mechanically, this is a self-hosted website to track learning. When the user adds a new topic, it runs a dedicated Claude code skill to generate the lesson plan using sub agents to research and compose each module. When completed, a final check reviews for discontinuity. Runtime AI work should use the Claude CLI, with one session per module. The sessions should be scoped such that they can only read and modify the module files, but don't get bogged down with excessive tools or the full codebase. Follow progressive education principles when possible. Deviate only when they would violate the spirit of the exercise.

F1.title: Topic intake
paths: happy (valid subject+level+purpose)
empty subject rejected
resubmission of a topic already `ready`
diagnostic skipped
diagnostic reveals substantial prior knowledge (affected modules flagged `test-out-eligible`)
material uploaded or pasted (subject pre-filled from it, units listed back, F2 given it as evidence)
unparseable file — damaged, password-protected, or not the format its name claims (refused by name, the paste path offered, and everything else typed into the form kept)
scanned PDF with no text layer (refused *as a scan* specifically — we do not OCR and say so — with the paste path offered)
material far larger than one course (kept to the cap, the learner is told what was left out rather than it being trimmed in silence, and lessons are written from the sections that match them)
material that contradicts the stated level (both kept: lessons stay at the level the learner chose and the disagreement is said once, not enforced)
acceptanceCriteria: submit creates a topic record in `queued` state
duplicate subject+level warns before resubmitting
form disabled fields re-enable instantly on submit (optimistic), job status polled/streamed separately
purpose and diagnostic transcript (if any) are stored on the topic record and readable by F2
skipping the diagnostic proceeds straight to generation with no penalty or nag
submitting with no material creates the topic on the existing path — no source directory, no source rows, no change to what F2 does

a topic created with material stores the extracted text and the original upload under that topic's `source/` directory and one `SourceDocument` row per piece of material, and both are removed when the topic is deleted
material whose title names a subject pre-fills the subject field, and text the learner typed into that field survives any later upload
extraction never opens a network connection and never invokes a provider
a PDF with no extractable text is refused with a message that says it is a scan and names the paste box, and no topic is created from it
a path that would resolve outside `<dataRoot>/topics/` is refused before any byte is written
F1.scale: topics=50, modules per topic=12, diagnostic exchanges=5, source documents per topic=10, upload=25 MB per file, extracted text kept=2,000,000 characters per document

F2.title: Curriculum research & generation
paths: happy (curriculum generates end-to-end as a branching graph)
subject decomposes strictly linearly (chain produced, no artificial branches)
research finds no suitable outline (falls back to generic decomposition by subtopic)
a module session fails or times out (topic marked `needs-attention`, partial modules kept, retry offered)
discontinuity review finds a gap (the lessons it names are rewritten and the check re-run; topic flips to `ready` when the loop converges, and the residue is logged when it does not)
a finding names no lesson this topic has (nothing to rewrite, so no further check is paid for)
graph defect (the edge is dropped or the island opened, and the correction is logged rather than noted)
a course longer than one prep window (the whole plan is stored, the first window is written, and the rest waits for the next authorised pass)
the outline comes back missing a unit the material names (the unit is inserted into the plan in the material's own order, displacing filler rather than being dropped)
research finds no outline at all but material exists (the material's own units and order become the plan, rather than the generic subtopic fallback)
material longer than a session's context (chunked and viewed, never truncated in silence; the omission is stated in the prompt)
the index says a document exists and the disk does not (the course runs on the documents that are readable, and the missing one is logged)
acceptanceCriteria: every module has learning goals, a warm-up problem, an explanation (link xor generated text), and an evaluation before topic flips to `ready`
the module graph is acyclic with ≥1 entry module, and stores explicit prerequisite edges (not an implied linear order)
a capstone spec referencing the driving question exists before topic flips to `ready`
discontinuity review runs exactly once per set of lessons, on the pass that finishes the course, and its findings are resolved by rewriting the lessons they name rather than shown to the learner
a module session cannot read/write files outside its own module directory

when the learner brought material, every unit it names is covered by at least one module in the generated graph, and the modules the material does not name are still added where the subject requires them
no session is handed more of the material than its budget allows, and any session reading an extract is told so in its own prompt
F2.scale: modules per topic=unbounded (floor 6, or the number of units the material names up to 60, typically 10-30), material read per research session=12,000 characters (scope digest), per authoring session=6,000 characters (excerpts), chunk=4,000 characters, lessons prepared per pass=10, subagent sessions per topic=modules + 1 research + 1 capstone spec + 1 discontinuity review + a ceiling of 2 repair rounds of 3 lesson rewrites and 1 re-check
